headline: Jamaat-e-Islami expresses regret over attack on journalists in Dhanmondi
summary: The party vows to take strict organizational action against any activists found involved in the assault on media workers during a protest.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami has decided to review an incident where journalists were allegedly assaulted while performing their professional duties in Dhaka's Dhanmondi.
The assault occurred around 8:45 am on Tuesday following a protest programme by Jamaat activists regarding the 77th founding anniversary of the banned Awami League.
Reports indicate that Mahfuzur Rahman Shishir of Dainik Sokal and Maruf Hossain of The News were injured, while at least 10 other journalists were harassed.
Central Publicity and Media Secretary Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair described the attack as "unexpected, unwanted and regrettable," expressing deep regret over the incident.
Zubair stated that the party will conduct an internal review to identify those responsible and will take strict organizational action against any activists if their involvement is proven.
The party suggested the situation may have been triggered by "overly enthusiastic individuals or outside provocateurs" after the peaceful conclusion of the protest.
Dhaka South City Jamaat Assistant Publicity Secretary Abdus Sattar Suman visited the injured journalist Shishir to offer condolences, calling the incident a result of a misunderstanding.
caption:
At least 10 journalists were harassed and two injured in Dhanmondi. Jamaat-e-Islami now vows action against those responsible.

Jamaat-e-Islami has decided to review an incident where journalists were allegedly assaulted while performing their professional duties in Dhaka's Dhanmondi.

The assault occurred around 8:45 am on Tuesday following a protest programme by Jamaat activists regarding the 77th founding anniversary of the banned Awami League.

Reports indicate that Mahfuzur Rahman Shishir of Dainik Sokal and Maruf Hossain of The News were injured, while at least 10 other journalists were harassed.

Central Publicity and Media Secretary Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair described the attack as "unexpected, unwanted and regrettable," expressing deep regret over the incident.

Zubair stated that the party will conduct an internal review to identify those responsible and will take strict organizational action against any activists if their involvement is proven.

The party suggested the situation may have been triggered by "overly enthusiastic individuals or outside provocateurs" after the peaceful conclusion of the protest.

Dhaka South City Jamaat Assistant Publicity Secretary Abdus Sattar Suman visited the injured journalist Shishir to offer condolences, calling the incident a result of a misunderstanding.

headline_marked: 31 [[tea estates at high risk]] of labour unrest, says Commerce Minister
headline: 31 tea estates at high risk of labour unrest, says Commerce Minister
summary: The National Security Intelligence (NSI) identified the gardens due to unpaid wages and management chaos following the disappearance of some owners.
details: Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muqtadir informed Parliament that the National Security Intelligence (NSI) identified 31 tea estates as high-risk for labour unrest in a special report dated May 18.

The unrest is primarily driven by unpaid wages. The Minister noted that following the events of August 5, 2024, some tea garden owners fled, leading to management chaos and failure to pay workers' salaries.

The high-risk estates include Tarapur, Premnagar, Bijoya, Patkhola, Madhabpur, Madanmohanpur, Kurma, Champaray, Burjan, Chharagang, Kagagul, Gulni, Lobhachhara, Lakkatura, Daldali, Kewachhara, Imam, Bawani, Noapara, Deundi, Lalchan, Chandichhara, Parkul, Satchhari, Phultala, Mathiura, Rajnagar, Ajgarabad, Muraichhara, Mirtinga, and Deorachhara.
To address the crisis, the Bangladesh Tea Board and district administrations formed committees to restart closed gardens like Burjan and Phultala, ensuring wages and benefits for workers.
Financial grants from the Tea Board's worker welfare fund have been provided to pay arrears. Currently, operations at Burjan and Phultala tea gardens have returned to normal.
For 12 gardens under the National Tea Company (NTC), the government arranged special exports of unsold tea stocks to secure the payment of workers' outstanding wages.

The Minister emphasized that the government remains committed to worker welfare, providing rations, free healthcare, primary education, housing, and various allowances including maternity and pension benefits.
